feed.subtitle: Stajich Laboratory at UC Riverside studies the evolutionary genomics of fungi, including their interactions with microbes, plants, and animals, extremophile fungi, and biological soil crusts.

entry.title: Rhodotorula mucilaginosa DH4148 genome published
entry.content:
Juhita Dhar, Prince Amoah, and Jason Stajich are co-authors, with Nicole Loeven and Deborah Hogan, on a new paper in Microbiology Resource Announcements: Draft genome sequence of basidiomycete yeast Rhodotorula mucilaginosa DH4148 from a patient with fungemia.

Rhodotorula mucilaginosa is a basidiomycete yeast with ecological importance and growing clinical relevance. The paper reports a high-quality de novo genome assembly of strain DH4148, which was isolated from a patient with fungemia.

entry.title: orthoSynAssign preprint posted
entry.content:
Cheng-Hung Tsai, Carolina Piña Páez, and Jason Stajich have posted a new bioRxiv preprint, orthoSynAssign: refine orthogroups using synteny information. The software is available on GitHub at stajichlab/orthoSynAssign.

Accurately identifying orthogroups is crucial for precise phylogenetic reconstruction, but clustering-based methods often generate complex, many-to-many orthogroups that include confounding paralogs. Incorporating synteny offers a robust strategy to refine these clusters into high-granularity, single-copy orthologs. orthoSynAssign is a user-friendly, high-performance rewrite of the orthogroup refinement tool OrthoRefine, combining an intuitive Python interface with a core computing engine written in Rust. This hybrid architecture makes installation and data parsing straightforward and keeps computation efficient.

Evaluated against the Yeast Gene Order Browser (YGOB) dataset, orthoSynAssign substantially improved the area under the precision-recall curve. Multi-threading benchmarks across 193 Eurotiomycetes genomes confirmed strong scalability, drastically reducing runtime while keeping a bounded, thread-independent memory footprint. orthoSynAssign provides a reliable and scalable framework for high-throughput phylogenomic workflows.

entry.title: Lab papers from March to October 2025

link.title: Lab papers from March to October 2025

entry.content:
A roundup of papers from the middle and later part of 2025 with lab members and collaborators.

Fungal pathogens and antifungal resistance

  • Giant transposons promote strain heterogeneity in a major fungal pathogen (mBio). Emile Gluck-Thaler, Robert Cramer, Aaron Vogan, and colleagues, including Jason Stajich, analyzed 519 Aspergillus fumigatus strains and found 20 distinct giant transposons that generate genomic heterogeneity, mobilizing genes with roles in biofilm-related virulence and biosynthetic gene clusters.
  • Coordinated regulation of Mdr1- and Cdr1-mediated protection from antifungals by the Mrr1 transcription factor in emerging Candida species (mBio). With Deborah Hogan’s lab at Dartmouth and Carolina Piña Páez, this work used CUT&RUN to define the Mrr1 regulon in Candida lusitaniae, showing that Mrr1 coordinates two multi-drug transporters and identifying a conserved binding motif.
  • Morphological and genetic characterization of novel Sarocladium spinificis strains in association with Coccidioides posadasii (bioRxiv preprint). A collaboration with Bridget Barker’s lab on a Sarocladium strain that suppresses Coccidioides growth.
  • Comparative Genomics Reveals Intra and Inter Species Variation in the Pathogenic Fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Genome Biology and Evolution). From Mark Yacoub’s PhD work on the amphibian pathogen.

Chytrid cell biology

  • Dynamic remodeling of centrioles and the microtubule cytoskeleton in the lifecycle of chytrid fungi (Molecular Biology of the Cell). With Tim Stearns’s and Lillian Fritz-Laylin’s groups, this study uses RNA-sequencing and expansion microscopy to show how centrioles and the microtubule cytoskeleton are remodeled as chytrids grow from zoospore to multinucleate coenocyte.

Extreme environments, soils, and microbiomes

  • Increased aridity is associated with diversity and composition changes in the biocrust mycobiome (bioRxiv preprint). Kian Kelly, Xin-zhan Liu, and colleagues examine how aridity shapes fungal communities in biological soil crusts.
  • Draft genome sequence of an uncultured archaeon from Antarctic endolithic communities (Microbiology Resource Announcements). Claudia Coleine and colleagues.
  • Soil drivers of fungal, bacterial and plant diversity in contaminated Southern Californian sites: Implications for dryland bioremediation (Science of the Total Environment). A survey of seven contaminated Southern California sites with Tania Kurbessoian, which identifies native plants that accumulate copper and soil factors that shape microbial communities, as candidates for dryland bioremediation.
  • Celebrating the fifth edition of the International Symposium on Fungal Stress (ISFUS) (Fungal Biology).

Genomes, tools, and data

  • Kingdom-wide CRISPR guide design with ALLEGRO (Nucleic Acids Research). A UC Riverside collaboration with Ian Wheeldon’s and Stefano Lonardi’s labs and Xin-zhan Liu. ALLEGRO uses integer linear programming to design compact sgRNA libraries targeting over 2,000 fungal species, with edits confirmed in four yeasts.
  • A roadmap for equitable reuse of public microbiome data (Nature Microbiology). Proposes a Data Reuse Information (DRI) tag tied to an ORCID so data creators can ask to be contacted before reuse.
  • A haplotype-resolved chromatin landscape connects cis-regulatory variants to trait variation in Citrus (BMC Genomics). With Danelle Seymour’s and Susan Wessler’s labs, including Talieh Ostovar and Jinfeng Chen. A locally phased mandarin genome links haplotype-specific chromatin states to allele-specific gene expression and fruit traits.
  • Draft genome of Conoideocrella luteorostrata ARSEF 14590 and Genome annotation of Aspergillus melleus strain CBS 546.65 (Microbiology Resource Announcements). Two genome announcements.
  • Activation of the Trichodimerol Pathway through Deletion of mcrA in Marine Penicillium rubens YAP001 (ACS Chemical Biology). With Clay Wang’s lab at USC, activating a secondary metabolite pathway to produce sorbicillinoids and trichodimerol.
entry.summary: A roundup of papers from the middle and later part of 2025 with lab members and collaborators.

entry.title: Papers from early 2025
entry.content:
A look at the first publications of 2025 that include lab members and collaborators.

  • Absolute abundance unveils Basidiobolus as a cross-domain bridge indirectly bolstering gut microbiome homeostasis (ISME Journal). A collaboration led by Mitra Ghotbi and Donald Walker at Middle Tennessee State University, with Kian Kelly, Leila Shadmani, Julissa Perez-Marron, Joey Spatafora, and Jason Stajich. The study applies absolute abundance profiling, using the DspikeIn framework, to bacterial and fungal gut microbiomes across amphibians and reptiles. It identifies core taxa that relative abundance hides, and suggests Basidiobolus acts as a connector between microbial modules in the gut network.
  • Fungal impacts on Earth’s ecosystems (Nature). A broad perspective with 33 authors on the roles fungi play across Earth’s ecosystems.
  • Section-level genome sequencing and comparative genomics of Aspergillus sections Cavernicolus and Usti (Studies in Mycology). A genome sequencing and comparative genomics study of two sections of the genus Aspergillus.
  • Assessing the Evolutionary Trajectory of Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Conserved Genes in Seagrasses and Aquatic Close Relatives (bioRxiv preprint). Cassandra Ettinger, Jennifer Arroyo, and Jason Stajich examine whether genes conserved for arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis are retained in seagrasses and their aquatic relatives.
entry.summary: A look at the first publications of 2025 that include lab members and collaborators.

entry.title: Congratulations Talieh Ostovar
entry.content: Congratulations to Talieh Ostovar who defended her PhD on June 28, 2024 on her project focused on plant comparative genomics in the genus Boechera as well as a project on the Citrus genome with our lab. Dr Ostovar was primarily advised by Liz Waters at SDSU but was co-advised in our lab through the UCR-EEOB Joint Doctoral Program with SDSU.

entry.title: Congratulations Cassie for winning CEPCEB Postdoc Award

link.title: Congratulations Cassie for winning CEPCEB Postdoc Award

entry.content:
Congrats to Cassie who was awarded the 2022 CEPCEB Postdoc Award.

Cassie was awarded the CEPCEB 2022 Outstanding Postdoctoral Researcher recognizing her excellence in research. This was exemplified by nine publications in 2022. Cassie has also been a terrific mentor to undergraduate and graduate students in the the lab and has lead multiple collaborative projects that achieved new findings but also helped teach students about metagenome pipelines and interpretation. She was a primary mentor for #NSURP and #RISE students the past two summers which have lead to two preprinted manuscripts.

This summer Cassie was also awarded an NSF Ocean Science fellowship to study transitions of plant associated fungi from terrestrial to aquatic plants focusing on sea grass. Congrats Cassie!

entry.title: Congratulations Dr Tania Kurbessoian
entry.content:
Congratulations to Dr. Tania Kurbessoian who completed her PhD work at the end of 2022. Tania was an integral part of the lab advancing new culturingi projects, a thoughtful and giving student mentor, and a key person in our data analysis of black yeast fungi. The lab greatly benefited from her efforts to keep the wet lab efficient for molecular biology, microbiology, and genomics techniques.

Our IG lab photo some dinner fun which captured a slice of some of the lab community that Tania helped establish.
